He took his rifle and he told him to make a dive for it, head first. And he said: He knows how to swim. And the young man was covered in blood. All we could do was to watch. We couldn't say anything. And that was what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would now request that the next exhibit be shown to the witness. And this is an intercepted conversation. And we'd request that this be played in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mujkic, you heard this conversation on Sunday. As you will recall, it caused you some distress. If you need time, just indicate that.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ MUJKIC
utterances.text: No. On Sunday I really had no idea what would be said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the intercept would get Exhibit number P381. The transcript would get Exhibit number P381.A. And the translation gets Exhibit number P381.A.1

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not -- I do not hear any translation at this moment. Mr. Gaynor --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English booth now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Stop for one second the tape to be played. I didn't hear any English translation. That means that neither English nor the French transcripts will contain the text of this intercept. So therefore, could we restart. Could we receive English translation, so that it will then also be translated into French. I can't control that, but ... Could we restart it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]. "Bakir ALISPAHIC: Hello. Ljubisa: Yes. Please go ahead. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Is it Mrki? Ljubisa: No, this is Ljubisa. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Well, Ljubisa, is Mrki there? What's up there? Ljubisa: Nothing. Who is that? Bakir ALISPAHIC: This is Bakir. Ljubisa: Oh, Bakir. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Where is Mirko? Ljubisa: He was here a moment ago. He went out. He will come in a minute. I think that he's somewhere in front of the door. Hang on a second, please. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Hello. Bakir ALISPAHIC: It's Bakir. What's up? Where are you? How are you? Mirko KRAJISNIK: Are you all right? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Damn, I'm not all right. Mirko KRAJISNIK: So what happened? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Well, I got worried. Mirko KRAJISNIK: What happened? Did he die, damn it? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes, he did. They were fighting but they could not, damn it. Mirko KRAJISNIK: One woman said to me -- so I was telling her not to talk a lot before these people because he had always been honest and surely I'm afraid that someone of the people took this --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Gaynor, I do not receive any French translation on the French channel. And since for the completeness of the records of the -- in English and in French, we really need to have all languages there. On the French channel I heard B/C/S rather than any translation in French. So could we perhaps -- I apologise, Mr. Mujkic, but we have some technical problems with the translation. Could we restart again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Bakir ALISPAHIC: Hello. Ljubisa: Yes. Please go ahead. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Is it Mrki? Ljubisa: Yes [as interpreted]. Ljubisa. Bakir ALISPAHIC: What's up there? Ljubisa: Who is that? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Bakir. Ljubisa: Oh, Bakir. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Where is Mirko? Ljubisa: He was here a moment ago. He went out. He will come in in a minute. I think that he is somewhere in front of the door. Hang on a second. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Hello. Oh, Bakir. Bakir ALISPAHIC: How are you? Mirko KRAJISNIK: How are you? Are you all right? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Damn, I'm not all right. Mirko KRAJISNIK: So what happened? Bakir ALISPAHIC: He got me worried. Mirko KRAJISNIK: What happened? Did he die, damn it? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes, he did. They were fighting. But they could not, damn it. This woman said to me --"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no interpretation. I cannot hear anything.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Mirko KRAJISNIK: You know I was telling her not to talk a lot because of these people. They'd always been honest and surely I'm afraid that some of these people to -- excuse me. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Let me just answer this. Well, I don't know Mirko. I really feel sorry for him, as if he were my brother. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Me too. Bakir ALISPAHIC: He was a good man, you know. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Real good man. Bakir ALISPAHIC: I called you yesterday to tell you. Mirko KRAJISNIK: You know, well, damn it. I went up there for -- what's it called? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Jasenk -- Mirko KRAJISNIK: Jasenkovic. That guard is Haris Jasenkovic. He is the treatment [as interpreted] of this state security. They have to carry out some investigation. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Well, Kijac and other others eat shit. Mirko KRAJISNIK: I don't know who it was. Believe me, though, the guys from Rogatica. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Really? Mirko KRAJISNIK: Not here. I was left that [as interpreted]. I asked yesterday. That guy Mladic was supposed to come last night. I told Momo that it should be unconditionally solved and that he had to meet your people today. Some commission and I don't know who else was supposed to come on behalf of the SDA party to talk. As they are supposed to -- so they went to meet them and I will call later to check what happened, you know. Bakir ALISPAHIC: So in Rogatica, but not here? Mirko KRAJISNIK: No, not here. Up there. That's why I went. Believe me, I went three times, but it's hard to talk to those people up there. Everybody wants to carry out something on his own. That's it. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Mirko. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Yes. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Several days ago your godfather [as interpreted] went to see him. I mean Ramiz Mujkic. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Ramiz Mujkic? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Which godfather? Bakir ALISPAHIC: He's the brother of Esma. You know her, the one who used to work in the army. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Yes. But what do you mean, 'godfather'? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Godfather. I asked you the other day when you were absent. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Okay, it was Nikola. Bakir ALISPAHIC: So I believe that he went to visit him there. I asked him to do that. Mirko KRAJISNIK: To visit who? Bakir ALISPAHIC: This Ramiz. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Ah, the guy who was -- Bakir ALISPAHIC: Wounded. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Okay. Wounded. Good. Bakir ALISPAHIC: So please, what could we do in order to give that man out? He would lose his leg. Remember his father, he also lost his leg. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, see, we have arranged an exchange for him. Bakir ALISPAHIC: His son was killed. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Really? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes, I swear to God. So, please, he is the only one left. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Listen, please. I know that we have agreed on this exchange, but those exchanges have been taking place in such a wishy-washy manner that, believe me, I am ashamed. People get you involved. I was involved accidentally. Not as the commission, but everybody comes here expecting I can help them with something and because of Momo and, I don't know, because of me; I know some people. And then you agree on everything. Believe me, I have not learnt in my life to agree on something that I could not carry out immediately. I cannot understand that. And every time here someone is hiding behind something it's easy to say shooting, whether or not one of the other side is the easiest [as interpreted]. Wouldn't you say they were shooting? Whatever. They could not come. That's not right, my friend. Bakir ALISPAHIC: So what can we do as far as Ramiz is concerned? Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, I will tell you. I mean, I will not interfere in that, but they told me that some exchange was agreed for Ramiz. Bakir ALISPAHIC: When was it arranged? Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, I heard that before I went for a trip I left the day before yesterday. Bakir ALISPAHIC: See the man is still here. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, I know he is. With the exchange should -- it involves 73 men from Ilidza and those from Mabzeran [phoen] did not take place. So, something should have happened in Hadzici today, but it did not. Then Ilijas and Breza. I was calling that guy Filip Vukovic up there to call me so I could tell people there was no connection and they did not answer the phone. A big exchange was arranged, but nothing happened. It was agreed that guy Prazina, what was his name, this young man, for a guy here, a corpse for a corpse, and even that was not done. That's horrible. Believe me, I swear. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Well, I don't know. Mirko KRAJISNIK: There is this other neighbour of mine, Cuprija. I agreed on an exchange with him and I really have to carry out what was agreed upon. You see what I'm saying. I mean, here, but I cannot do it. I do not have this kind of experience. They tell me to go to the Butmir bridge, to the Butile bridge, where we did an exchange for those six persons, but nobody is there. People simply start hiding. They do not answer the phone when you're persistent, damn it. Bakir ALISPAHIC: I don't know, I would ... Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, you check for this guy, Mujkic, and check what is going on, so why it came to a standstill. Well, you know, so perhaps there is somebody on your side who could arrange it. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Well, I want to tell you there is somebody. People from Trnovo will call me tonight. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Yes. Bakir ALISPAHIC: There are many detainees up there. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Who? Serbs, or Muslims as well? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Both. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Both? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Well, yes. So let us solve this. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, I was up there yesterday, I mean concretely, since Filip asked me to do him a favour, that guy Karkin, to go there to check, to agree with our people to exchange as many people as possible. It is not possible to endure this any longer and people are getting killed. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Of course, why are you going to check with this? [as interpreted]. Mirko KRAJISNIK: I'm really sorry about this Kalibri, damn it. Bakir ALISPAHIC: This, believe me, is just as if he were my brother. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Oh. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Everybody loved him. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Milan Plakolovic came to see me yesterday, but I was not there. He was asking for me up there. They probably didn't want me to tell him, and they certainly would not tell me. They said "Mirki" from up there. They do not know that I kept in touch. And this woman said to me, I don't know how to tell you this. I felt as if she poured boiling [as interpreted] water on me. Bakir ALISPAHIC: I am truly sorry. Mirko KRAJISNIK: He was an extremely honest man, believe me. So was he buried there in Sarajevo? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes, he was. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Does his family know? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Nobody knows. Well, his father knows. They are here. Mirko KRAJISNIK: And what about his wife? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Let me tell you, his father had two heart attacks and God knows how he will end up. This is really very sorrowful. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Did you check anything about Djino? Bakir ALISPAHIC: Somebody was coming to the barracks. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Viktor Bubanj. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Viktor Bubanj. Mirko KRAJISNIK: I know. One young man was coming, Milicevic. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Allegedly he is not there because he called me. Are you talking about Bato? Mirko KRAJISNIK: Yes, Bato. Bakir ALISPAHIC: He said to me he's not there. Well, that's it. Mirko. Now, that's how it is. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Oh, damn. Bakir ALISPAHIC: I asked some people here were in Dobrinja today. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Yes. Bakir ALISPAHIC: To try to check it there. Mirko KRAJISNIK: And then how come that we cannot do it? There is one young guy. He got killed in Dobrinja, and he was probably digging trenches and a shell killed him. And now you cannot exchange a dead man, I say. And you cannot exchange a dead man. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Well, who is that? Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well one guy, Vukicevic. Right here from my village. He had an apartment there. Sorry. Sorry. Vukic. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Where is he now? Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, he was buried in front of the hospital somewhere in Dobrinja. I don't know where in that hospital he's buried [as interpreted]. Yes. Somewhere there in front. It was on the 13th and I asked to check whether there were some Muslims. And he is dead, if there is an equivalent. If they need a live person, it doesn't matter. You know what it means. It was their only son. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Yes. Mirko KRAJISNIK: He stayed in his apartment to keep it. They picked him up and sent him to dig trenches, and that's what happened. You get killed and that's it. Life is the cheapest thing in the world. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Of course, it seems to me that nobody values life any more. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Of course. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Nobody. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Well, let me tell you. After I talk tonight I will talk to you tomorrow regarding this Jasenkovic. As soon as I check about this Mujkic, I will let you know. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Okay. Do that, please. Mirko KRAJISNIK: All right. Bakir ALISPAHIC: Bye-bye, kid. Bye. Mirko KRAJISNIK: Cheers. Farewell. Bye."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkic, that intercept appears to refer to you and to your son. Could you tell the Judges --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ MUJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: -- when -- do you know whether your son is dead?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ MUJKIC
utterances.text: My son is registered as a missing person. There are 16 persons from Ahatovici about whom we don't know where their bones are even. One of them is my son. So I don't know anything of his fate. I don't know where his bones are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did anyone confirm to you in 1992 whether he was alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ MUJKIC
utterances.text: No. No. No document was given to me. And in the records, he is still registered as a missing person. In order to be declared dead, there has to be a paper, a document, on the basis of which he would be declared dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I've just got two more questions for you. First is: Can you tell the Judges the impact of that not knowing about your son has had on you personally?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ MUJKIC
utterances.text: It's a very hard question. I'll try to give you an answer. Though you're all human beings. You will understand me. There is no radio in my house. We play no music in the house. Every religious holiday, when the family is supposed to gather together, we weep. Every wedding is a day of weeping, because my wife and I are like two tree stumps now. But according to any logic, we should be playing with our grandchildren now. My sister's house is across the street from mine. My mother lives in it now. She is 80 years old and she always needs some kind of help. Whenever I go to see her, I always expect my Elma and Edim, my sister's children, that they call out to me and say: Uncle. But they're no longer there. So you can conclude what kind of a life I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mujkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkic, I would have one question for you at this stage before we adjourn, and that is the following: You told us about the mass graves marked 3, 4, and 5 on the map. You told us that in one of these mass graves, 16 bodies were found. Were they ever identified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the bodies that were exhumed from all the mass graves, including the mass grave in Sokolina. All these bodies were identified except for two. Two men from Bratunac who were buried at the cemetery in Visoko where the exhumation was carried out. And they were buried there and marked as "NN." All the persons killed from the settlement of Ahatovici were identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. And my next question related to this one would be: You told us that in Ahatovici most of the population was Muslim. Were any of the identified bodies Serb or Croat, or of another ethnicity than Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Mujkic, unfortunately, as perhaps it has been told to you already, this Chamber is not sitting the coming days, and I do understand, but please correct me when I'm wrong, Mr. Gaynor, that you'll return at a later date in order to be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We don't -- are not entirely sure when the Defence wants to do that. It might be a matter of liaison between the witness and VWS and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we do not know exactly yet when that will be, but, as I would say in every court, both parties have the right to put questions to you. So when you return, the Defence will put questions to you as well. Meanwhile, I'd like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given and the testimony you still have to give once you return to The Hague. I understand that perhaps it's not easy to do that. Usually it's only for one day and then you return in court. This might be for a longer period. But I nevertheless have to instruct you that this is not a subject for conversation with whomever. Mr. Mujkic, so we'd like to see you back at a date still unknown. I can -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just to clarify the record. I just want to reassure

utterances.speaker: MR. MUJKIC
utterances.text: There won't be any contact between the Defence and you before you come back. It will be done through the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'll hear when you -- and I take it that -- take care of your personal situation as well, as when to come. Mr. Mujkic, so therefore usually I thank witnesses for having come to The Hague, and that's usually at the very end of their testimony. I'd like to thank you for having come to The Hague this first time and expect you to be back, and I'm fully aware that it would have been better if you would have had to come only once to The Hague and not two times. Apologies for that, but I can't change it at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no problem. I will come whenever necessary. Because it is in my interest for the truth to be revealed and to give evidence about the situation that unfortunately did take place. I will come whenever you summon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Mujkic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the parties, we'll not sit tomorrow, we'll not sit the day after tomorrow. If there are no procedural issues to be raised at this moment -- or are there any?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just very quickly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because the interpreters, we have stolen already ten minutes of their time.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that's why I propose to do it very quickly, Your Honour. I can indicate that while we've been in court, Ms. Dixon has spoken to Mr. Stewart and he has indicated he will be able to deal with that additional witness next week. I think apparently his words were he's not happy but he's fine with it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And the other aspect, of course, Your Honours, as a housekeeping matter, is I did raise on the 4th of October in court the question of my seeking to withdraw on the basis of inadequate time given to the Defence and issues of inadequate resources and inequality of arms. Your Honours will be aware, of course, that I filed that withdrawal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you were so friendly to send a copy of your filing to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I just wanted to ensure -- to place that on the record that I'd also copied it to Your Honours and Your Honours have received that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have received that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the only thing I still have to do, and it takes us perhaps one and a half or two minutes, is to give an oral decision on the admission of the transcripts of Witness 629 into evidence under Rule 92 bis. The Prosecution sought to tender into evidence, pursuant to Rule 92(D) bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The transcripts of Witness 629's prior testimony in the Brdjanin case in relation to the events in the municipality of Kljuc. In its response of the 18th of October, 2004, the Defence has stated no objection in relation to the admission of Witness 629's evidence but has indicated that it wishes to cross-examine this witness. The Prosecution, at transcript page 5604, has agreed that the -- that cross-examination of this witness would be appropriate should his evidence be admitted. The Chamber has examined this material for compliance with the tests for admission under Rule 93 bis and is satisfied that it meets the requirements set out in that Rule. Notwithstanding the name of the accused appears in this evidence at transcript pages 11445, 11453, 11455, 11485, 11486, and 11487. The Chamber does not consider that these references can be interpreted as relating to the acts and the conduct of the accused. However, taking into account the submissions of the parties and the nature of the evidence as a whole, the Chamber deems it appropriate to call Witness 629 for cross-examination. And that's what will happen next week. We'll adjourn until next Monday. Mr. Registrar, could you guide us as to the time and the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At a quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, this same courtroom, number 1. We stand adjourned.
